system_prompt:
You are a fourth-grade student taking the TIMSS mathematics test for students in your grade. Do your best on each question, as you would on a real test, using the mathematics you have learned in school so far.

The pictures, figures, and graphs of the test booklet are described in words, and its tables are written out. When a question asks you to draw, mark, shade, label, or fill in something on a figure, graph, or table, describe exactly what you would draw or write, and where. When a question asks you to show your work or explain your answer, include the work or explanation in your answer. For a multiple-choice question, choose one option.
user_prompt:
These 2 questions belong together and follow one another in the test booklet.

## Question 1

Bill is arranging squares in the following way:

[Image: Figure 1 with one column of two squares, Figure 2 with two columns of two squares for each column, and Figure 3 with three columns of two squares for each column.]

A. Draw Figure 5.

Figure, described in words:
Three figures made of identical adjacent square cells are shown in a row, each labeled underneath:
- Figure 1: 1 column of 2 squares (a 1-by-2 grid).
- Figure 2: 2 columns of 2 squares each (a 2-by-2 grid).
- Figure 3: 3 columns of 2 squares each (a 3-by-2 grid).

## Question 2

Bill is arranging squares in the following way:

[Image: Figure 1 with one column of two squares, Figure 2 with two columns of two squares for each column, and Figure 3 with three columns of two squares for each column.]

B. How many squares would Bill need to make Figure 16?

Answer: ____

Figure, described in words:
Three figures made of identical square tiles arranged in a grid: Figure 1 consists of 1 column of 2 squares stacked vertically, labeled "Figure 1". Figure 2 consists of 2 columns of 2 squares each (a 2-by-2 square), labeled "Figure 2". Figure 3 consists of 3 columns of 2 squares each (a 3-by-2 rectangle), labeled "Figure 3".

Answer each of the 2 questions.

answer_1.description: Your answer to question 1, as you would write it in the test booklet, with any work, explanation, or description of a drawing that the question asks for.
answer_1.title: Answer 1

answer_2.description: Your answer to question 2, as you would write it in the test booklet, with any work, explanation, or description of a drawing that the question asks for.
answer_2.title: Answer 2

output.answer_1: Figure 5 would have 5 columns, each column made of 2 squares stacked vertically, forming a 5-by-2 rectangle of 10 squares. I would draw five vertical pairs of squares side by side: the first column has 2 squares, then 2 squares in each of the next four columns, arranged in a row, so the figure is 5 columns wide and 2 squares tall.
output.answer_2: Figure n has n columns of 2 squares, so it has 2 x n squares. For Figure 16: 2 x 16 = 32 squares. Answer: 32
